question: In your own words, explain how photoelectron spectroscopy (PES) tells us about electron arrangement inside an atom.
answer: PES uses high-energy photons to eject electrons from atoms. High binding-energy peaks represent core electrons; low binding-energy peaks represent valence electrons. The number of peaks indicates distinct occupied subshells, and peak height indicates how many electrons are in each subshell.
